app_root_note: Root against which protected_app_paths are resolved: RELATIVE to the project root (e.g. '.' or '..' when application code lives in a sibling repo). Never absolute - this file is committed, and '/Users/<name>/...' resolves nowhere on the next machine (audit A20 fails on it). guard_pre_tool.py warns when a protected path does not exist on disk.
protected_app_note: MUST be filled by onboarding: application code paths relative to app_root, e.g. ["src", "backend"]. This is P-00: writes into these paths are blocked by a hook. An empty list means the rule is not yet enforced by code.
test_locations_note: Where THIS project keeps its tests inside the application code, as the person named them at onboarding: folders or file patterns relative to app_root, written like protected_app_paths - 'src/**/__tests__/', 'src/**/*.spec.ts', 'src/legacy/checks/'. A trailing '/' or a last segment with no wildcard means that folder and everything in it; '*' stays inside one folder and '**' crosses folders, so '*.spec.ts' is only files directly in app_root and '**/*.spec.ts' is everywhere. What is listed here is not application code: the protected_app_paths guard lets test files there be written, and every other path under protected_app_paths stays closed. An entry that covers a whole protected_app_paths entry, an absolute path or one with '..' opens nothing and is named once per session. Empty means the person has not named any: the usual test names in references/test-path-markers.json are only a suggestion at onboarding and a fallback for recognising tests, never a permission; a test inside the application code then needs the person's word per story (waiver.py --block "protected test path: <pattern>"). Recorded with the person's words through project_decisions.py (field /test_locations).
tests_root_note: Root of the test repository, relative to the project root (never absolute - audit A20) - set when tests live in a repo separate from the application code (qa-scout treats app repo and test repo as distinct inputs).
cases_root_note: Where THIS project keeps its test-case documents, relative to the project root (never absolute - audit A20). Filled by onboarding: discovery looks for an existing store (a test-cases/ directory, case files named by an id, a TMS link) and topic 1 ASKS when it finds none. Empty means the project keeps no case library of its own, and the factory keeps cases per story under qa-factory/artifacts/<TICKET>/work/test-cases/ - the behaviour of every config written before this key existed. Set, it is the one place cases are written and read: qa-case-designer writes <cases_root>/<area>/<case id>.md, the coverage map counts from there, and a case written anywhere else is refused. It may not point inside protected_app_paths - the factory never writes into application code, whatever a config says.
case_id_form_note: The shape of a case id in THIS project, as a template (or a list of templates): {ticket} is any ticket key (at most once), {nnn} is the case number (exactly once), everything else is literal text - e.g. "{ticket}_TC_{nnn}" for TP1-13877_TC_001. A literal may not contain whitespace, '--' or any of / : # , [ ] \ * ? " < > | (they separate areas, instances and scopes). Filled by onboarding from the strategy's Case ids line; empty means TC-{nnn}, the form every config written before this key existed uses. The default TC-{nnn} is always recognised as well, so cases already written keep their ids and a store can hold both. An id is the case's file name and its front-matter id; stored ids are never rewritten. A form the factory cannot read is ignored (readiness names the problem) and only TC-{nnn} is used.
code_repos_note: Application repositories when the code does NOT live under this root — the shape of a dedicated test repository. One entry per repo: {name, path, default_branch}. `path` is relative to the project root (this repository), e.g. '../testproject1', so the config stays portable across machines. An absolute path is a DEFECT, not an option: audit A20 fails on it, because this file is committed and '/Users/<name>/Projects/testproject1' resolves nowhere for the next person to clone the test repo. A checkout that cannot be reached relatively is recorded as a deferral, not as an absolute path. Filled by onboarding topic 1, which must ASK when discovery could not locate the checkout. readiness.py's app_repo capability takes any existing entry here as evidence the application code is present; with several repos, app_root is their common parent and protected_app_paths are relative to it. Empty plus app_root '.' means nobody has said where the application code is — not that it is here.
test_command_templates_note: Shell command templates with a <test-file>/<test-id> placeholder, filled in by run_suite.py. 'quiet' is the default mode for every role that runs tests (common-rules.md); 'one_test' backs the --detail <test> lookup, no re-run.
adapter_capabilities_note: Verified capability matrix by adapter_id. An adapter absent from this matrix is unknown and cannot make a profile ready merely because its name appears in config.
profiles_note: Extensible execution contours. Each entry contains profile_id/revision, roots, adapter_id/version, required capabilities, dependency_ids, execution_prerequisites ({runtime, package_manager, dependency_state, hook_executables}), named commands ({kind, argv, cwd, scope}), selector/reporter/quality_gates contracts, conventions/environment/data/ownership refs, and versioned adapter extensions. Only selected profiles participate in readiness.
implementation_repos_note: One record per relevant repository: repo_id, role, local_path, remote_identity, source_ref resolved before source_sha, immutable source_sha, execution_profile_id, write_target, working_branch/base_sha for write targets, readiness_evidence, and content_hashes for local changes.
managed_dependencies_note: On-demand catalogue only; presence never authorizes installation. Each dependency declares dependency_id, upstream_source, exact_version_or_revision, integrity, location, executable, capability, consumer, owner, status (ready/unavailable/unsupported/unknown), and probe_evidence. Readiness verifies the executable and command cwd instead of trusting status alone. Activate and provision only when a selected profile needs it.

environment.note: How a role obtains the environment for the story's default/local stand (filled by onboarding). Empty = not configured: env_probe.py says so out loud instead of a role digging out credentials itself. An empty env_file means values come from the process environment (CI secrets, a secret manager). Secrets listed in secret_keys are never printed. integrations are the stand's prerequisite services ({name, keys, owner, health_url?}) — env_probe reports their state with an owner. `access` is HOW the project reaches the stand, learned at onboarding and proved by one real login (every value is a key NAME or a URL, never a secret): kind harness_command | local_login | oidc_password | bearer_env | none; `unauth_status` are the codes an unauthenticated request answers by design (302 to an identity provider, 401); `login_probe` is the proof (user key, status, date). A key the code reads but the env file does not carry belongs in integrations[] with `required_by` (areas or profiles), never in secret_keys - a missing integration blocks an area, a missing login key blocks the stand.

integrations.name: aws-integration
required_by: api: cloud tools and Parameter Store loading

integrations.name: azure-integration
required_by: api: Azure DevOps datasources and tools

integrations.name: github-integration
required_by: api: git datasources and VCS tools

integrations.name: other-integration
required_by: api: tests that read these names

integrations.name: sandbox-integration
required_by: api: data-management and sandbox tool tests

test_data.accounts_by_role: Default user from AUTH_USERNAME/AUTH_PASSWORD; extra users created per test through the admin API (LocalUserUtils) on the local stand
test_data.seeds: Per-test resources named with get_random_name(); harness-managed seeded persistent entities for Sonar, XWiki, ServiceNow, InfluxDB and Report Portal tests
test_data.generators: Dataclass test-data modules under tests/test_data and tests/ui/test_data, yield fixtures in tests/conftest.py
test_data.pii_and_masking: No real data in the tests (confirmed by the team)
test_data.cleanup_owner: Fixture teardown per test; the factory cleans the local docker stand when needed; the containers are recreated only when really necessary

test_data_note: Onboarding topic 3, one key per lifecycle fact so a missing one is VISIBLE instead of absent from prose. Every key carries an answer or the literal 'unknown' — 'unknown' is a recorded answer, silence is not. accounts_by_role: where role accounts come from. seeds/generators: how a fresh dataset is created (fixtures, factories, a seed script, a shared seeded stand) and the tooling that produces it. pii_and_masking: whether any of it is real data and the masking rule — data marked PII never reaches an artifact verbatim (common-rules.md). cleanup_owner: who resets or cleans, and when. shared_records: the entity types a test may depend on instead of creating, the ONLY exception to common-rules' 'your own test data'; an empty list means there is no exception. What may safely be BROKEN on a particular stand is per-stand and lives in environments[].safe_to_break, not here.

environments.name: local-docker
environments.bring_up: docker compose from ../../docker-compose.yaml (backend built from main); already running, recreating the containers is slow and done only when needed

environments_note: One entry per named stand: {name, base_url, bring_up, credentials_by_role, safe_to_break}. --env at story launch selects one by name; the default comes from onboarding. See environments.md for the resolution order and safety rules.
adapters_note: Reachability only — see adapters-read.md. 'file' is the built-in ticket adapter for fixtures/evals (--ticket-file). READING goes through ticket.direct_api (base_url, auth_type, secret_ref, username_ref for basic_token — jira-direct-access.md), which ticket_adapter.py uses whatever method says; readiness proves it before S1. ticket.method says how this session reaches the tracker for WRITING — command | mcp_tool | agent | skill — and is separate from ticket.name, which says WHICH tracker it is; 'agent'/'skill' need ticket.invoke. A tracker reachable only through this session (mcp_tool/agent/skill) is not_configured for reading: the S1 role holds none of the orchestrator's tools. Empty method is inferred from whichever of command/mcp_tool is set, for configs written before the key existed. ticket.project_keys lists tracker project prefixes known in advance (e.g. ["APP", "OPS"]): a key with such a prefix becomes a source without a probe; any other prefix costs one project lookup, not one per key. ticket.key_pattern (a bare regex for one ticket key, for example [A-Z]{2,6}-[0-9]+) is read only for the `file` adapter and for a tracker kind references/adapter-forms.json does not hold; vcs.delivery_commands (for example ["bb pr create"]) adds commands that deliver a change to the ones that file already holds, so the delivery gate stops them until the delivery verdict allows it. What actually gets WRITTEN to is controlled separately by external_writes below.
external_writes_note: bugs: markdown | jira. cases: markdown | xray | testrail | zephyr. markdown is the default and a first-class channel, not a degradation. A non-markdown channel writes a proposal file; external_writes.py executes exact authorized case descriptions after Gate A and results/bugs after Gate B. channels.<name> = {method: command|agent|skill, command|invoke: ...} says HOW that channel is delivered; a legacy commands.<name> string reads as method 'command'. An agent/skill channel is delivered by the orchestrator (exit 4 + --record), never by a role. See adapters-read.md.
requirements_sources_note: Verified or unresolved requirement sources. Each entry records source_id, kind, locator, method, invoke_or_command_ref, status and evidence_refs. Locators never contain credentials.
strategy_documents_note: One record per strategy document: relative path, provenance (factory_created, pre_existing or legacy_unknown), editable permission, decision_ref and source_refs. Permission is exact-file only.
factory_may_edit_strategy_note: Legacy compatibility permission only. true permits edits solely to qa-factory/strategy/test-strategy.md and qa-factory/strategy/framework-rules.md; false/absent is propose-only. New per-file strategy_documents grants take precedence and never authorize a directory.
tracker_write_note: The RIGHT to create an issue is probed by tracker_write.py without creating one: direct API -> mypermissions + createmeta; an agent channel -> channels.<name>.writes (true|false) plus one question the orchestrator asks and records. bugs_project defaults to the first adapters.ticket.project_keys entry. probe.max_age_h is how old a stored answer may be at S0, gate_b_max_age_h at the gate B rehearsal.
sizing_note: sizing.py weighs every verifiable requirement by the priority its impact class maps to (impact_scale) - never one multiplier for a whole story. All keys optional; an omitted tier keeps the default.
dispatch_windows_note: controller stage-scope cuts S5 into windows of at most ui_window_cases cases whose plan row is e2e-ui, or api_window_cases others (execution.s5_window_cases overrides the non-UI size when set) - one dispatch each, never merged. mechanical_rounds is how many mechanical fixes the critic worded (a sleep, a raw locator) go back to the author per window; each is closed by the author's own green run on the new bytes, never by another critic, and spends no repair cap - only a repair whose cause is test_defect spends the cap of two.
dispatch_note: dispatch_liveness.py: how long a role's subagent transcript may stay silent before the dispatch counts as abandoned, and how long a dispatch with no transcript may wait before it counts as never launched. abandoned_after_s is also how long a host receipt that is not terminal, with no other evidence, counts as a live launch: a fresh receipt is alive, an older one is unknown and only a person's release closes it. native_completion_grace_s is how long after a Codex worker's own clean task_complete its stop hooks may still send it back: a worker that completed less than that ago counts as alive, an older completion counts as a return. It also bounds how long a rollout cut mid-row still counts as alive after its last whole row, so changing it changes both. A host that keeps no transcripts answers unknown and nothing is closed by absence.
gate_rehearsal_reporter_note: Before gate A the rehearsal runs ONE existing test through each execution profile's own commands.one_test, with the report written into the OS temp directory and never into the task's evidence: a profile whose run leaves no report the factory can read becomes a stand-gap card (kind reporter, id RP-<profile>) carrying the flag that cures it - karma/ng --reporters junit plus karma-junit-reporter, jest --reporters=jest-junit, dotnet --logger "junit;LogFilePath=<path>" - instead of stopping the first real run of S5. reporter_probe_test names the test: one string for all profiles, or {"<profile_id>": "<node id or file>"}; empty means the first node id of the gate's own collect for pytest, else the first test file under the profile's cwd. reporter_timeout_s caps that run; skip_reporter turns the step off, and waiver.py --stage S5 --block "stand gap: RP-<profile>" passes the card on a person's word.
gate_rehearsal_executor_note: Before gate A the rehearsal resolves the launcher of every execution profile S5 will need (poetry/npx wrappers, a scripts/*.sh and the tools it names); a missing one is one question with three answers - install it here, name an environment where the factory can run it, or the person runs those cases (only that answer hands anything over, recorded as waiver.py --stage S5 --block "executor unavailable: <profile>"). skip_executor turns the step off.
gate_rehearsal_preconditions_note: Before gate A gate_preflight.py checks every case's `preconditions` (flag, data, account, variable, service) on the stand: an env check reads the env files the runner really loads (environment.env_files, else env_file, else what the conftest loads, else .env at the test root), an http check is one anonymous GET. Unmet or uncheckable is one grouped question to the person per case; a check that cannot run is the factory's, never the person's.
gate_rehearsal_note: gate_preflight.py collects the project's EXISTING tests through its own run command before gate A (toolchain and imports alive). skip_collect turns it off for a project whose conftest must not run at a gate.
turns_note: Turn budget, counted per dispatch by the host's agent_id and separately for the orchestrator's window (guard_pre_tool -> turn_budget.py): soft = the call on which a role is first told how many tool calls it has made, repeat = how often the notice comes back after that. It is a notice, never a refusal - the same call again proceeds. Cost inside one window grows as the square of its turns, so the number is worth saying in the middle of a dispatch rather than after it.
budget_note: Per-story ceiling. null = no ceiling; warns once at each warn_at fraction, stops and asks at 100%. A person's word passes it: waiver.py --stage <S> --block "story budget".
prompts_note: `slices` decides how a role's own rule files reach it. `inline` (the default) injects their contents: the layer exists because 0 of 290 dispatched subagents in the donor measurement ever opened a file they were told to read. `on_demand` injects `references/slices/<role>/index.md` instead - the paths and one line of what each carries - and the role reads what its work touches, which takes about 16 KB off every dispatch (41,590 -> 24,942 characters for the code critic, measured). That is the largest single saving available in a dispatch prompt and also the one most likely to cost quality, so it is opt-in: turn it on, run a story, and compare the artifacts with `stage_compare.py` before leaving it on.
handoffs_note: The handover form between two roles (handoffs/README.md). `story_step start` writes it from the contract and `finish` refuses it when the role did not fill it, or filled it and left it incomplete - the form IS the handover, and a receipt nobody wrote is what this exists to stop. Set `required: false` when the project does not want the form; `finish --ignore-handoff`, a person's word recorded like any other block, passes one dispatch without changing the project.
judge_note: A System One judge for the S1-S4 judgments (references/judge.md). provider none sends nothing anywhere; typesafe sends the questions and the ticket text they are about to api.typesafe.ai - the project owner's decision. mode shadow journals answers without acting on them; on lets a decided answer replace the role's judgment. The key is read from the named environment variable only.
pipeline_note: stop_after gate_A or gate_B ends every story once that gate is decided; null runs S0-S9.

api.note: written by `runtime_probe.py --suggest --write`. {python} and {plugin_root} are resolved on the machine that runs the probe, so this entry is the same on every machine. Only {argv, cwd, timeout_s} are read.

execution_s5_window_note: s5_window_cases: how many NON-UI cases one S5 automation window takes (stage-scope windows[]). null = dispatch.api_window_cases (4). A larger window (8 = one window per area) means one automator dispatch learns the repository once and its repair rounds go back to the same dispatch; e2e-ui rows keep dispatch.ui_window_cases whatever this says.
execution_node_ids_note: Before a pytest launch run_suite.py checks the asked node ids against a real --collect-only: an id with exactly one real spelling (pytest-playwright prepends the browser: [chromium-...]) is resolved silently with a note, a truly missing one is refused with the nearest ids and nothing is launched. runtime_probes maps a profile id (or *) to {argv, cwd, timeout_s} whose output is a provenance JSON - read by the gate A rehearsal, by S5 before a story's first `--mine` run, and by manual capture. In `argv`, `{python}` stands for the interpreter that runs the factory and `{plugin_root}` for the installed plugin; both are filled in where the probe runs (`runtime_probe.resolve_argv`), so a committed config means the same on every machine, and an absolute path written there is run as written and reported by audit A20. `cwd` absent is the project root, `timeout_s` absent is 30.
sandbox_note: Seconds ONE red-probe call may spend installing dependencies into its disposable clones (a request's `sandbox_setup` rows, kinds in references/sandbox-setup.json): the worst-case timeouts of the rows of a call must add up to at most this. The role's Bash tool stops a call at 600 s, and an install cut off that way leaves a half-made clone and a running npm, so the default stays below it. Raise it only if the probe is run in the background; absent means 540.
telemetry_note: telemetry_hook.py prunes qa-factory/state/telemetry/ itself, throttled to once a minute: the newest keep_commands command pairs and keep_days days of hook files survive (7375 files and 27 MB after five days on one project).
guards_note: An evidence .log/.junit.xml up to raw_log_free_bytes reads freely (Read and shell); above it the guard refuses and names the summary's error_head and run_suite.py --detail. 0 = no log reads freely.
stand_health_note: stand_health.py watches finished runs: same_failure_cases different tests failing in a row with one normalized line, or a run over slow_factor x the median of comparable runs (never below slow_min_s), puts stand_signal with one plain sentence into the run summary - repairs stop and the person hears the sentence.
format_changed: git diff --name-only <base>...HEAD -- '*.py' | xargs poetry run ruff format
format_note: Two keys, because a role holding only one picks wrong. format_changed formats ONLY the files this story touched (the project's formatter over `git diff --name-only <base>...HEAD`) and is the only formatting a role may run. format_all is the project's wide command and is a SEPARATE cleanup, never part of a story. On TP2-2520 the configured command was the wide one: format:check reported drift in 39 frontend files while the story changed one test file, so running it would have rewritten other people's work inside a QA merge request. When a project offers only a wide command, onboarding derives the narrow one rather than leaving the choice to a role.
records_policy_note: Where the factory's SHARED records go - obligations.md, factory-backlog.md, strategy/* - which accumulate across stories. `with_story`: they travel in the story's merge request. `separate` (default): committed apart from the story, so a reviewer of one ticket is never handed the history of three others. `local_only`: not committed at all. The story-local artifacts/<TICKET>/ folder is unaffected and always travels with its story. Asked at onboarding; the default is the answer that cannot surprise a reviewer when nobody answered.
run_dependency_files_note: run.dependency_files lists extra files, by name or by path relative to the folder the test command runs in, whose bytes decide whether an earlier proof or run still stands: the factory's own list of dependency files does not name every project's, and a file listed here that is present costs at most one extra run or rehearsal, never a missed change. A config without the key, or with an empty list, behaves as before: the factory's own list only.
run_stand_note: With parallel false the stand takes one run at a time: a second run_suite.py launch waits up to stand_wait_s on a project-level lease (stand_lease.py) instead of failing both. A lease whose process is dead is taken over; only a person frees a live one: stand_lease.py --release --env <name> --reason "...".
run_reporter_note: How a test run becomes machine-readable. reporter: pytest | junit-xml | trx | none — pytest is equipped by run_suite.py itself (--junitxml is added); every other framework writes the report from the project's own command (dotnet: --logger "junit;LogFilePath=<path>" or "trx;LogFileName=<path>"; karma/ng: --reporters junit; jest: --reporters=jest-junit) and report_path says where, relative to the project root. An empty reporter is inferred from the command. A run with no report is recorded as not_executed however green its log is, and a failed test cannot be told from a broken launcher — which is what a .NET and a Karma run cost one project: totals in the log, not_executed in the record, results rebuilt by hand from raw logs.
run_levels_note: run.levels maps a pyramid level (unit | component | api | integration | e2e-ui) to the path patterns of the tests that live at it, e.g. {"api": ["tests/api/**"], "component": ["frontend/**/*.test.tsx"]}. It is ONLY for tests the factory did not write: a factory test carries its level through its plan row. What matches nothing is shown as 'level not recorded' - the board never guesses a level from a test name.
dod: All tests of the story and of the regression are green, bugs found are documented, and every requirement is checked.
impact_scale_note: Impact class maps directly to priority and severity. Numeric area multipliers are invalid and require an onboarding decision; they are never translated automatically.

cost.note: Full-session usage including the orchestrator. Exact model rates resolve from approved rate_overrides first, then the bundled exact-id catalogue. Legacy project model_prices remains readable in old configs but is never generated. Missing exact price keeps tokens and a partial known subtotal; it never guesses a family rate. external_agent_forms: optional rows for an agent CLI other than testproject1, in the shape of references/external-agent-calls.json (id, command_re on the lower-cased command, consumer_re with one group, call_id_prefix, invocation_method, provider, service, unknown_consumer_label). A row that reuses a package id or prefix, or breaks the grammar, is skipped and named in the cost file's forms_problem. A config without the key, or with an empty list, behaves as before: the package's own forms only.

retro_note: Share of a story's priced cost the orchestrator itself may spend on dispatching, re-assembling requests, repeated acceptances and holding context before the retro and the Factory tab call it a finding about the factory. A fraction, not a percentage.
